sources.observation: Current free homebuyer guide explains septic systems and recommends pre-purchase inspection.
sources.interpretation: Problem exists; a general buyer guide is already free.
sources.limitations: Does not measure book purchases.

sources.observation: A direct 2026 Kindle title, Septic System Risk for Homebuyers (ASIN B0GRBXQFN7), promises inspection interpretation and risk framing.
sources.interpretation: The proposed advantage is already claimed by a current entrant.
sources.limitations: Visibility, reviews and rank were insufficient for a sales estimate.

sources.observation: Published inspector examples quote roughly $740–$1,500 depending on vehicle, excluding add-ons.
sources.interpretation: RV buyers visibly spend on inspection and receive detailed reports.
sources.limitations: Association profile of one inspector; not a market average.

sources.observation: Buyer guidance says to request scope, sample report and points of inspection.
sources.interpretation: There is a concrete pre-purchase information job.
sources.limitations: Provider association has an incentive to promote inspections.

sources.observation: 371 results; visible direct/near-direct books include two June 2026 buyer guides at about EUR12–15, a 2020 inspection title with 15 ratings, and older buyer guides with 50–71 ratings.
sources.interpretation: Book format is established but the accessible advantage is weak.
sources.limitations: Query count is noisy; ratings and prices are observations, not unit estimates.

sources.observation: Reserve studies combine physical and financial analysis and can affect special assessments; CAI supports disclosure to buyers.
sources.interpretation: A consequential buyer document and problem exist.
sources.limitations: Policy statement, not consumer purchase data; rules vary by state.

sources.observation: Five exact results, including direct buyer-due-diligence products published Aug 12, Aug 25, Sep 5, Sep 6 and Sep 7, 2026; visible prices roughly EUR11–19 and one title had 2 ratings.
sources.interpretation: The exact shelf filled rapidly; no distinct accessible advantage remains in the tested thesis.
sources.limitations: Very new titles have little traction history.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid
sources.observation: Official current guidance explains comparison of non-standardized aid offers and costs.
sources.interpretation: Problem and decision deadline are real.
sources.limitations: Does not establish paid book demand.

sources.observation: A free upload-based financial-aid decoder launched in March 2026.
sources.interpretation: A proposed normalization workbook faces a stronger free substitute.
sources.limitations: Vendor announcement; adoption not disclosed.

sources.observation: AAEP advises buyers to invest in a customized purchase exam and communicate intended use to the veterinarian.
sources.interpretation: Problem and professional spending are established.
sources.limitations: No price or book-demand evidence.

sources.observation: Reporting guidance makes the veterinarian responsible for exam scope while suitability remains the buyer's decision.
sources.interpretation: A buyer aid would require careful veterinary boundaries and expert review.
sources.limitations: Professional guidance, not a buyer product study.

sources.observation: A professional assessment is intended to identify cost-effective energy improvements.
sources.interpretation: Homeowners buy an assessment to prioritize spending.
sources.limitations: Older guide and no current service-price data.

sources.observation: 16 results; visible books focus on DIY audits, energy efficiency or professional training. A 2024 DIY guide was about EUR10.75; a 2023 title had 13 ratings; a June 2026 playbook had no visible rating.
sources.interpretation: Adjacent book buying exists, but demand for post-audit report-to-action workflow is unproved.
sources.limitations: No BSR history and query matching is imperfect.

sources.observation: AARP reports one-third of family caregivers use paid help and explains agency versus direct-hire trade-offs.
sources.interpretation: Families visibly pay and face a consequential vendor-selection job.
sources.limitations: The cited share comes from AARP/NAC research; it does not measure book demand.

sources.observation: Free guidance and a contract-question checklist already exist.
sources.interpretation: A paid product must normalize actual agency proposals and answers, not repeat generic questions.
sources.limitations: Free alternative quality not tested with buyers.

sources.observation: Exact query returned one direct 1995 family guide with 1 rating. Adjacent paid caregiving formats include a 2024 toolkit with 162 ratings and current paperback logs around EUR7–10.
sources.interpretation: Book-format spending exists adjacent to a weak exact shelf; proposal comparison is not visibly served.
sources.limitations: Search placement and ratings do not establish conversion for the proposed product.

sources.observation: ISA publishes multiple professional sample tree-risk reports.
sources.interpretation: Homeowners can receive structured reports but interpretation is safety-sensitive.
sources.limitations: No consumer spending or book-demand measure.

sources.observation: Mobile food vendors must obtain a permit and pass local vehicle inspection before opening.
sources.interpretation: Trigger and deadline are strong.
sources.limitations: County-specific rules make a national book volatile.

sources.observation: AARP provides a free caregiver financial workbook and reports substantial caregiver out-of-pocket spending.
sources.interpretation: General caregiver organization is well supplied for free; agency-proposal comparison must be narrower.
sources.limitations: Out-of-pocket care spending is not publishing spend.

sources.observation: ABYC says a prepurchase survey produces a technical written report for purchase decisions, negotiation, insurance and lending; buyers should ask the surveyor to explain unclear findings.
sources.interpretation: The buyer job and professional spend are real, but safety and technical interpretation belong to qualified professionals.
sources.limitations: No book-demand or survey-price evidence.

sources.observation: Shelter standards call for accurate dated medical records covering findings, tests, procedures and treatments.
sources.interpretation: A record-handoff job exists, but buyer dissatisfaction and publishing spend were not established.
sources.limitations: Professional shelter standard, not consumer demand evidence.

sources.observation: Official conservation guidance provides a detailed condition-report checklist and specialist terminology.
sources.interpretation: Condition reporting is a real structured job; safe interpretation remains specialist work.
sources.limitations: No consumer spending or book-demand evidence.

sources.observation: The toolkit recommends an independent specialist conservator and treats condition reports as important transaction documents.
sources.interpretation: A consequential art-purchase job exists but creates specialist dependency.
sources.limitations: Industry guidance, not publishing demand evidence.
